findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: Let \Gamma = \operatorname{Gal}(N/k_{\mathrm{cyc}}) = \langle \tau \rangle \simeq \mathbb{Z}_p, and let M = \mathbb{Z}_p g_1 \oplus \mathbb{Z}_p g_2 with \tau(g_1) = g_1 and \tau(g_2) = g_2 + g_1. The submodule X = \mathbb{Z}_p g_1 has trivial action, but for any h = g_2 + c g_1 with c \in \mathbb{Z}_p, \tau(h) = h + g_1 \notin \mathbb{Z}_p h, so no \Gamma-stable complement H to X exists in M whenever the extension class is non-trivial in \operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathbb{Z}_p[[\Gamma]]}(\mathbb{Z}_p, X). Moreover, X(\tilde{k})_{\operatorname{Gal}(\tilde{k}/k)} is not known to be a free \mathbb{Z}_p-module, which was assumed in [p32-0]. Both steps are invalid and invalidate the proof of Proposition 4.2.1 in §4.2.3 and consequently Theorem 1.1.1(II).

evidence.text: where blank entries are all zeros. This implies that, by adding some linear form of \( g_1, \ldots, g_{m-2} \) to \( g_{m-1} \) and \( g_m \), we can take a \( \operatorname{Gal}(N/k_{\text{cyc}}) \)-subgroup \( H \) in \( \operatorname{Gal}(C/N) \) such that \( \operatorname{Gal}(C/N) \simeq H \times X(\tilde{k})_{\operatorname{Gal}(\tilde{k}/k)} \) as a \( \operatorname{Gal}(N/k_{\text{cyc}}) \)-module. Then \( \operatorname{Gal}(C^{H}/N) \) is isomorphic to \( X(\tilde{k})_{\operatorname{Gal}(\tilde{k}/k)} \) as \( \operatorname{Gal}(N/k_{\text{cyc}}) \)-modules, where \( C^H \) is the fixed field by \( H \). Now, let us denote by \( F \) the maximal abelian subextension in \( C^{H}/k_{\text{cyc}} \). Then, since \( N/k_{\text{cyc}} \) is a \( \mathbb{Z}_p \)-extension, we see that \( \operatorname{Gal}(F/N) \simeq \operatorname{Gal}(C^{H}/N)_{\operatorname{Gal}(N/k_{\text{cyc}})} \), which is non-trivial. This means that \( F \) is an unramified abelian \( p \)-extension which is not contained in \( \tilde{k} \). However, this contradicts our assumption that \( L(k_{\text{cyc}}) = \tilde{k} \). Therefore, \( X(\tilde{k})_{\operatorname{Gal}(\tilde{k}/k)} \) is trivial, and so is \( X(\tilde{k}) \). This completes the proof of Proposition 4.2.1.
